input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "preservation",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariant only describes the already-swapped outer regions (k < i and k > a.Length-1-i). It says nothing about the untouched middle region i..a.Length-1-i, so after the havoc of the loop Dafny no longer knows that a[i] and a[a.Length-1-i] still hold their original values. The swap therefore cannot be shown to place old(a[a.Length-1-i]) at i and old(a[i]) at a.Length-1-i, so the invariant is not preserved, and the postcondition (which also needs the middle element unchanged for odd lengths) fails. Fix: add an invariant stating the middle region is unchanged: forall k :: i <= k <= a.Length-1-i ==> a[k] == old(a[k])."}
EOF
sed -i '9a\        invariant forall k :: i <= k <= a.Length - 1 - i ==> a[k] == old(a[k]); //The middle region is untouched' program.dfy
dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
I fixed `program.dfy` and it now verifies: Dafny reports "2 verified, 0 errors".

**Diagnosis** (written to `diagnosis.json` before the edit): the problem was a loop **invariant** that failed **preservation**. The existing invariant only described the outer parts of the array that had already been swapped. It said nothing about the middle part the loop hadn't touched yet. So at each iteration Dafny no longer knew that `a[i]` and `a[a.Length-1-i]` still held their original values, and couldn't prove the swap puts the right values in place. The postcondition failed for the same reason: for odd-length arrays it needs the middle element to be unchanged.

**Repair:** I added one invariant saying the middle part is untouched:

```dafny
invariant forall k :: i <= k <= a.Length - 1 - i ==> a[k] == old(a[k]); //The middle region is untouched
```

The command still exits with code 2. That is because of style warnings in the original code, not proof errors. The warnings are for unneeded semicolons and for `requires a != null`, which is always true because `array<int>` can't be null. I left those lines as they were. If you want a clean exit code, removing them would get rid of the warnings without changing what the program does.
